_comment: Production overrides for the FishMMO Control Panel. Kestrel binds loopback only; TLS terminates at NGINX. Database credentials come from FISHMMO_DB_USERNAME / FISHMMO_DB_PASSWORD or /etc/fishmmo/db-secrets.env, and ConnectionStrings__NpgsqlConnection must be set (with Ssl Mode=Require) or the host refuses to start. Do not commit real credentials here.
_comment_smtp: Outbound mail. THIS process drains the email queue and sends; the LoginServer only enqueues (its own Smtp:DrainQueue is off). The password is a live sending credential and belongs in /etc/fishmmo/db-secrets.env as FISHMMO_SMTP_PASSWORD, never here. UseSsl=true performs STARTTLS on port 587; port 465 (implicit TLS) is NOT supported by this sender. Leave Host empty or at localhost to run with no relay - the drain logs once and idles.
_comment_sms: Outbound SMS. THIS process drains the SMS queue. No SMS gateway exists yet: the only provider is 'log', which writes each message (verification codes included) to the panel log and delivers nothing. Outside Production an empty Provider means 'log'; in Production an empty Provider leaves the drain idle and queued messages wait.
_comment_verification: Which channels this server verifies. A channel the player chose whose switch is off is marked proven without a code. Both off: every account is verified on creation (the same path as the development auto-verify). SMS 'delivery' is the log provider until a gateway exists.
_comment_beta: Closed-beta registration gate. When Enabled, registration requires a code redeemable for one of Programs (lowercase keys such as closed_beta; empty means any program). Panel sign-in is never gated, so players can redeem a code later.
_comment_auth_lockout: Sign-in lockout. The counters are shared with the LoginServer in the database, so these numbers must match the game's. A locked password step answers exactly like a wrong password; a locked two-factor step says until when.
_comment_two_factor_reset: Self-service two-factor reset for a player who lost the authenticator and every recovery code. It takes effect DelayDays after it is requested; signing in normally cancels it, and staff may shorten or cancel it.
